findings.title: An offline edit now keeps `pendingInit`, so a later adoption can silently replace the user's rename
findings.body: An offline edit used to delete `pendingInit` in every case. It now keeps it and sets `pendingIdentity` alongside it. When the folder comes back with an identity whose id this Mac doesn't know, `availability` now takes the adoption branch (lines 718-726). `Object.assign(entry, entryFromIdentity(...))` overwrites `name`/`color`/`initials` with the folder's values. That silently discards the rename the user made offline, even though the `editSavedOffline` toast had told them it would reach the folder. The branch also leaves `pendingIdentity` set. Before this change, the same case ended as `unavailable: different`. That was worse in a different way, so the new behaviour is arguably better overall. Still, nothing tells the user their edit was dropped. If the registry's newer name should win here, as it does in the `pendingIdentity` branch at line 670, apply the pending name and color after adopting. Otherwise, clear `pendingIdentity` in the adoption `refresh` so the flag doesn't outlive its meaning. This is the same scenario the owner already noted as a follow-up (a moved drive plus an identity written by another Mac), so it is rare.

contracts.action: Picking the folder the workspace already points at in "Change folder…" returns `unchanged: true`, and the renderer skips the "now points to the new folder" toast
contracts.equivalent_path: A real relocate: `registry.relocate`, or `relocateActive` for the active workspace, then `relocateFolder` probes, refreshes titles and broadcasts state
contracts.before_after: The early return comes after `relocateRefusal` and `checkRelocate`, so refusals still apply. `relocateFolder` still runs `reg.availability`, `refreshTitles` and `broadcastState` (which rewrites an identity file deleted by hand), and passes the flag on to the IPC result.
contracts.visible_effect: The dialog and Settings both call `onRelocated`, which returns before `showToast` when `unchanged` is set. Nothing is shown, and the dialog gets the current workspace view.
contracts.failure_mode: If the call rejects, both the dialog and the context show `relocateUncertain`, as before. A same-folder pick that `resolve` compares as different (for example a case difference that `samePath` accepts) falls through to the full relocate. That works, but it shows the toast.

contracts.action: An edit that couldn't write to the folder now keeps `pendingInit`, so a later "Change folder…" accepts a moved folder that has Kaipu items and no identity
contracts.equivalent_path: `availability`, which clears `pendingInit` only after it writes or adopts an identity
contracts.before_after: `pendingIdentity` is set alongside it. When the folder comes back without an identity, the probe writes one with the registry's edited name and clears both flags (lines 733-748). If the folder holds an identity with the same id, the `pendingIdentity` branch writes the edit but leaves `pendingInit` set. The registry stays consistent, because `pendingInit` only matters to `checkRelocate` and adoption.
contracts.visible_effect: The registry-relocate test checks that relocate is accepted after an offline edit. After the move, the probe writes `identity.json` under the registered id.
contracts.failure_mode: If the folder comes back holding an identity with an unknown id, the adoption branch overwrites the offline rename and leaves `pendingIdentity` set (reported as a finding).

structuredOutput.summary: This round does two things. Picking the folder a workspace already uses in \"Change folder…\" now returns `unchanged: true`, and the renderer skips the \"now points to the new folder\" toast for it. An edit that couldn't reach the folder now keeps `pendingInit`, so a later \"Change folder…\" still accepts a moved folder that has no identity. Both work as described, and the tests check the right things. One minor finding (consider): because `pendingInit` now survives an offline edit, the probe's adoption branch can overwrite the user's offline rename with the folder's identity without telling them, and it leaves `pendingIdentity` set. All earlier threads are addressed.
